title: High cardinality — written update
situation: In a technical discussion, a proposal uses customer identifiers as metric labels. You must write the decision accurately without overstating the evidence.
instructions: Write four sentences on what cardinality does to a metric store, the scale at which it breaks, and the alternative.

vocabulary.meaning: keeping the number of distinct label combinations bounded, because each combination becomes a separate stored series
the growth of stored time series when an unbounded value is used as a label, which degrades the whole metric store rather than one metric

expectedElements: The mechanism of series creation is explained
An order of magnitude is given, not just a warning
An alternative placement for the identifier is proposed
modelAnswer: Customer identifiers must not be used as metric labels, because each distinct label combination creates a separate stored series. A bounded label such as status produces a handful of series; a customer identifier produces one per customer, so a hundred thousand customers means a hundred thousand series for a single metric. The consequence is not a slow dashboard but a degraded metric store affecting every team. The identifier belongs in a log line or a trace, where per-request evidence is expected and priced accordingly.
commonMistakes: Stating the rule without explaining that each label combination becomes a series
Warning about cost without giving an order of magnitude
variants: Rewrite the update proposing where the identifier should go instead.
